title: Choice and consumption of animal or plant-based protein: Controlling experimentally and statistically for sensory stimulus aspects and food choice factors
author: Pohlmann

steps.title: Capture baseline demographics and traits
steps.instruction: At the start of the survey, record participants' biological sex and age, ask how many hours ago they last ate (0 = <1 h, 1 = 1 h, … up to 5 h) to estimate hunger level, and collect any enduring psychological measures needed for the hypotheses.

steps.title: Screen for allergies and eligibility
steps.instruction: Ask participants about food allergies; if the jerky will be consumed, confirm no relevant allergies and disclose the full ingredient list from the manufacturer.

steps.title: Select and pre‑test jerky stimuli
steps.instruction: Choose commercially available jerky products that are visually similar and differ only in the main protein source (e.g., beef, turkey, tuna, salmon, soy, textured vegetable protein). Pre‑test the selected products to verify that there are no significant taste differences before using them in the experiment.

steps.title: Prepare equal portions and label nutrition
steps.instruction: Cut or package each jerky product into equal portion sizes (e.g., 1 oz = 28 g). Average the caloric values and macronutrient contents (carbohydrate, fat, protein, sugar) across the three products and label each portion with the same caloric and nutritional information. Ensure the label format matches the example shown in Fig. 2.

steps.title: Randomize and present health information
steps.instruction: Display near‑identical health and nutritional information for each stimulus on the survey platform, randomizing the order of presentation for each participant. Optionally include processing covariates such as “I am familiar with nutritional labels” and “I am proficient at reading nutritional labels” (1 = strongly disagree … 5 = strongly agree) or record the time each participant spends on the information screen.

steps.title: Conduct choice task with limited sensory exposure
steps.instruction: Present the sealed jerky packages (or images of them) without allowing visual or olfactory inspection. Ask participants to choose the product they would like to sample. Keep tactile, visual, and aroma exposure delayed until after the choice is recorded.

steps.title: Provide sealed serving for consumption
steps.instruction: Give the participant the chosen jerky portion in a sealed container or bag (1 oz = 28 g). Allow them to consume the sample while keeping the container sealed until after consumption.

steps.title: Collect sensory evaluation
steps.instruction: After consumption, have participants rate the sample using the 12 semantic differential adjective pairs (e.g., –3 = “tasted bad” … 3 = “tastes good”, yuck/yum, disgusting/delicious, looks bad/good, tastes bad/good, looks inedible/edible, unpalatable/scrumptious, flavorless/flavorful, looks repulsive/appealing, smells bad/good, hard/tender, chunky/minced, dry/moist). Record each rating for later analysis.

steps.title: Weigh leftovers to infer consumption
steps.instruction: After the participant leaves, weigh the remaining jerky in the container. Subtract the leftover weight from the original 28 g portion to calculate the amount consumed. Link this value to the participant’s survey responses using a unique printed code attached to the container or plate.

steps.title: Collect post‑choice physical measurements
steps.instruction: After the choice and sensory tasks, ask participants to report their height and weight. Compute Body Mass Index (BMI) and predicted Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) from the self‑reported sex, age, height, and weight.

steps.title: Record additional covariates
steps.instruction: Gather self‑report data on physical activity (using a validated scale), current dietary restrictions (e.g., calorie‑restrictive diet), food involvement (using the food involvement scale), and meat‑avoidance intent (three yes/no statements: avoid red meat, avoid any animal flesh, avoid any animal product). Sum the meat‑avoidance statements to create the MAI score (0 = omnivore, 3 = vegan). Ensure logical consistency of responses, either manually or via survey logic.
